title: the librarian proves its own command line folds its system words
intention: The librarian's command line (cairn/devices/librarian/live.py _main) folds its first token so LOOP, Shelve and learn reach their branches and the rest of the line rides verbatim (ruled 2026-09-07, ticket e3cf75c6dc8f). Today that is measured only from cairn/tools/system_word/proofs/test_system_word.py:329, which imports the librarian, a RULE 1 breach. The librarian's own proof holds it here, so system_word's copy can leave.
why: Measured 2026-11-11: encapsulation_holds names cairn/tools/system_word/proofs/test_system_word.py:329 (cairn.devices.librarian). RULE 1: a ticket's proofs measure only that component, so the librarian's fold tooth berths with the librarian before system_word drops its copy.
traces_to: CLAUDE.md RULE 1; outline 2.3.7.1 (a device's public interface is the bus plus any tool it publishes); outline 17.13.1.
how: New proof cairn/devices/librarian/proofs/test_librarian_cli_folds_its_verbs.py stubs live.py's four branches (_loop, _shelve_collection, _learn, _summarize) at call time and drives _main with each verb lowercase, uppercase and capitalized; each must reach exactly its branch, and 'LOOP Once MiXeD Text' must hand the loop ['Once', 'MiXeD Text'] unchanged. No code change.

clauses.claim: each of the librarian's four verbs, typed lowercase, uppercase or capitalized, reaches exactly its own branch
the tokens after the verb reach the branch byte-identical

decisions.text: D1: the librarian's fold tooth berths with the librarian; system_word's copy leaves in its own ticket.
